TITLE: FIFO and LIFO Accounting
ALIASES:
DESCRIPTION: Covers FIFO and LIFO methods for inventory management and financial reporting assumptions.
SUMMARY: The document discusses FIFO and LIFO methods for inventory and financial matters. It explains how FIFO records the oldest inventory first, and LIFO records the most recently purchased items first. The conclusion notes that the difference between the two methods is called the LIFO reserve.
ORG: Internal Revenue Code || WHY: Directs how LIFO may be used if the taxpayer establishes no other way to value inventory.
ORG: Save LIFO Coalition || WHY: Argues in favor of the retention of the LIFO method.
ORG: International Financial Reporting Standards || WHY: Valuation principles are subordinated to the lower of cost or market valuation.
CONCEPT: FIFO
WHY: Mimics the flow of inventory by selling the oldest inventory first.
CONCEPT: LIFO
WHY: Records the most recently purchased items as sold first.
CONCEPT: LIFO Reserve
WHY: Is the difference between FIFO and LIFO inventory cost calculations.
FACT: If Foo Co. sells 210 units during November, the total cost of sales under FIFO would be $11,050. || SECTION: FIFO
FACT: Under FIFO, the total cost of sales for November would be $11,050. || SECTION: FIFO
FACT: The ending inventory under FIFO would be calculated at $5250. || SECTION: FIFO
FACT: Under LIFO, the total cost of sales for November would be $11,800. || SECTION: LIFO
FACT: The balance sheet would show $4500 in inventory under LIFO. || SECTION: LIFO
FACT: The difference between the cost of an inventory calculated under the FIFO and LIFO methods is called the LIFO reserve. || SECTION: LIFO
